figures.before: Why Occupied Facility Construction Requires a Different Operational Model
figures.alt: Occupied hospital expansion corridor with sealed ICRA partition, negative-air machine, clean hospital circulation, and organized temporary protection
figures.caption: Occupied construction has to preserve the daily function of the building while the work proceeds. Routes, separation, air, utilities, hours, noise, safety, communication, and releases become active project controls.

figures.before: Interim Life Safety Measures (ILSM) for Commercial and Healthcare Occupied Construction
figures.alt: Hospital life-safety coordination area with protected egress route, temporary construction separation, and clearly maintained corridor access
figures.caption: Temporary changes to building conditions need a deliberate life-safety response. Egress, protection systems, detection, signage, emergency planning, coordination, and the return to normal operation must be managed together.

figures.before: Dust and Contamination Controls: HEPA Filtration, Negative Pressure, Barrier Construction Specifications
figures.alt: Hospital corridor renovation with a sealed temporary containment wall, protected floor, negative-air equipment, and clean adjacent circulation
figures.caption: Containment is a complete control system: continuous barriers, pressure or air management, protected routes, cleaning, inspections, release criteria, and a response when the control is compromised.
